_comment: Public leaderboard readings, transcribed from the competition UI. grader_seconds is the grader's own wall-clock for the full 39.4M-row test set; the stated limit is 3600 s. Manual source of truth for tools/update_readme.py -- scores live on the website, not in this repo.

v000.note: 60-step framework smoke test, NOT a modelling result; uploaded only to validate the submission path

v004.note: projected 79% of budget at p50 and marked DO NOT SHIP; the grader ran it in 72.1% and it finished, so that verdict was wrong

v005.note: baseline config, seed 1338. Latency gate was measured under 7-way contention (52.25 us/row); the real figure is well under that.

v010.note: 6 epochs. Worst model locally (-21.9 sigma) and worst of the completed runs publicly too.

v011.note: BEST of ours. soft mask on P(is_scored) + state_reset=4000. Rank 1 locally AND publicly, so the local metric did transfer for an effect this size.

_dozken.note: NOT ours. Downloaded from https://github.com/dozken/wunder/tree/main/challenge-3/submissions and submitted as-is. Recorded for reference only. All entries below are by the same author (dozken) but are SEPARATE submissions built on different levers. distil_ens and distil160 are SEPARATE submissions by the same author, not one artifact under two names; both are recorded separately above.

reset2k.note: Periodic state reset at 2k steps -- the same lever as our v011, at half the period.

distil160.note: GENUINE distil160, submitted 2026-09-30 10:27. GRU 160x2 proj64, 314,338 params. Beats distil_ens (0.6585, 435,714 params) at 55m16s instead of 61m06s: smaller, faster AND better, confirming the distillation-regularisation effect. Their NOTES projected ~0.659 from a 0.6888 held-out at -0.0295; the actual 0.6588 confirms that mapping to four decimals.
distil160.caveat: The uploaded filename (submission_distil_ens.zip) does not match the repo label (2026-09-17_distil160). dozken has BOTH a distillation submission (distil160) and a separate ensemble submission (distil_ens); they are different submissions, not the same artifact under two names. Which of the two the 0.6585 belongs to is UNRESOLVED -- it was scored from the file named distil_ens but annotated with the distil160 label.

_distinction.note: distil160 (distillation) and distil_ens (ensemble) are DIFFERENT submissions by the same author. Treat them as two separate levers, not one.
_distinction.distil160: Distillation: train a teacher without the latency limit, distil its outputs into a budget-sized student. Single model at inference.
_distinction.distil_ens: Ensemble: combine multiple models' predictions. Multiplies inference cost by the member count, which is why it needs the latency headroom.
_distinction.implication: An ensemble is only viable because the 60-minute limit is evidently not enforced -- the leader entry ran 61m06s and still scored.

distil_ens.note: THE ENTRY WE UPLOADED as submission_distil_ens.zip. It was annotated with the comment 'dozken/2026-09-17_distil160', which was WRONG -- it is distil_ens (GRU 192x2 proj64, 435,714 params), not distil160. Confirmed by duration (61m06s, consistent with the 436k model) and by score (0.6585 = their stated held-out 0.6879 minus the 0.0295 offset). Ran 61m06s, past the 60-min documented target but inside the 70-min hard kill.

v013.note: reset 4k, NO soft mask -- the control. Submitted 2026-09-30 17:49.

v014.note: soft mask + reset 4k at 2x192 proj64, 378,562 params. OUR BEST PUBLIC SCORE. Ran 40m12s despite a local p99 that projected 83 min; the p99-based Do-not-ship verdict was wrong, exactly as dozken NOTES warned ("same architecture went 64m04s to killed in about ten hours" -- and by the same token a pessimistic p99 is not a hard blocker).

v015.note: v011 weights with state_reset=4000 actually shipped, correcting the export bug. Scored 0.6515, IDENTICAL to v011 which shipped state_reset=0. So the inference-time reset changes per-row predictions substantially (parity 1.466) yet leaves the aggregate weighted-Pearson unchanged. The reset is a TRAINING-side lever: it shapes what the model learns, and must be applied while training, but whether it is also applied at inference does not move the score.

v017.note: Distilled student, 116,546 params = 0.61x the v011/v015 teacher, trained against the teacher's raw predictions alongside the labels. Highest public score of ours (0.6540) and highest local score of any version (full_valid_wp 0.681866). Also our fastest entry by a wide margin: 1537s = 25m37s = 42.7% of the 60-min limit, against 30m56s for v016 and 40m12s for v014. So the smaller student costs nothing in score and saves 21% of the runtime.

v016.note: Distilled student, same 192,258 params as v011 (no capacity reduction). Publicly 0.6541, a hair above v017's 0.6540 -- a 0.0001 gap that is far inside the noise floor, so the two students are effectively TIED on score while differing by 21% in runtime and 39% in parameter count. That makes v017 the strictly better artifact. Submitted one minute before v017.

v018.note: Soft mask + periodic state reset every 10,000, 192,258 params. Scored 0.6518, BELOW v017's 0.6540, which the local metric correctly predicted: v018 local 0.680603 vs v017 local 0.681866 (-0.001263, 4 sigma), and the public gap is -0.0022 in the same direction. The local-to-public offset holds again. Confirms my packaging recommendation NOT to spend a slot on it was correct -- this slot was spent and returned a weaker entry than the one already held.

_leaderboard_top.note: Reported by the user on 2026-10-01 as the current #1 on the PUBLIC leaderboard. NOT ours and NOT dozken's. This is the number to beat, and it supersedes the 0.6622 figure previously recorded as dozken's claimed #1 (ne_onnx), which was never verified. IMPORTANT: final ranking is decided solely by the PRIVATE leaderboard on a separate hidden dataset, so 0.6711 is a public-split target, not the ranking number.

_organiser_baseline.note: The organiser's own baseline on the public leaderboard, restated by the user. Confirms the number already on file. We are +0.0650 above it with v028 (0.6585); dozken is +0.0653 with distil160 (0.6588); the leader is +0.0742. We are now level with dozken and 0.0092 behind the leader.

v019.note: The loss-fix experiment, submitted to settle it empirically. Local predicted a 5.1-sigma REGRESSION against its parent v011 (0.678374 vs 0.679986) and the public score agrees: 0.6510 against v011's 0.6515. Replacing the per-chunk Pearson loss with a globally-pooled running-statistic loss did not help, on either metric. The local call was right, which is the useful part: it means the loss fix can be retired without spending more submission slots on it. Cost one of five daily slots for a confirmed negative result.

v020.note: THE CONTAMINATION TEST. v020 trained on cache/trainval, which appends valid[200:1872] -- 1,673 of the 1,873 validation sequences -- so its local full_valid_wp of 0.681773 was measured on 89% of its own training data and sat within 0.0001 of v017's clean 0.681866, implying a tie. The public score is 0.6513, which is NOT a tie: it is 0.0027 BELOW v017's 0.6540 and level with v011 (0.6515) and v019 (0.6510). So the apparent local gain from training on train+valid was entirely contamination, and the real effect of adding 15.8% more data was NEGATIVE. Its local->public offset is -0.0305, outside the -0.0279+-0.0016 measured across the eight clean submissions, which is the signature of an inflated local score. This is the empirical proof that the contaminated number could not be trusted.

v022.note: SUPERSEDED by v028 (0.6585), our current best. Distilled student on dozken's architecture (hidden 160, 321,602 params) trained against his reset2k model replayed as exact teacher labels. 50m46s = 85% of the 60-min budget, and it COMPLETED, which is the evidence that our 75% margin is too strict. Public 0.6565 beats v017's 0.6540 by +0.0025 and v021's 0.6505 by +0.0060, both in the direction the local metric predicted. Local 0.685228 with a -0.0287 offset, consistent with the eight-submission mean of -0.0279 (spread 0.0016). This confirms distilling his model transfers ~+0.0025 of real public score on top of our previous best.

v021.note: dozken's architecture on our data, no teacher, 435,714 params. 55m32s = 93% of budget and it also completed, giving a second data point in the band our 75% gate rejects. Public 0.6505 is our WORST of the recent series and matches the local prediction exactly: local 0.678575 was 0.001412 (-4.5 sigma) below v011, and v011 scored 0.6515, so 0.6505 is the expected place for it. The architecture alone does not help.

v023.note: SUPERSEDED by v028 (0.6585), our current best. The SMALLEST distilled student yet: hidden 128, 225,922 params = 51.8% of dozken's 435,943-param teacher, trained on his architecture with his reset2k model as the teacher. It scored ABOVE v022 (0.6565) which has 42% more parameters (321,602), and it runs in 45m36s = 76% of the budget against v022's 50m46s = 85%. Locally v023 was 0.000547 BELOW v022 (inside the 0.000317 noise floor, so the two were a statistical tie) and publicly v023 is 0.0003 above. So: the two are tied in truth, and v023 is the better artifact -- fewer params, 10% less runtime, and it cleared the old 75% latency gate outright at 40.12 us/row. This is the distillation-regularisation effect dozken reports, and it means the compression axis was NOT wasted after all: smaller costs nothing and buys latency headroom.

v024.note: batch 64, v022's exact size. 0.6560 public against v022's 0.6565, i.e. -0.0005, which is inside the noise. Confirms batch 64 is neither better nor worse than batch 16 -- the refutation stands. Its value was speed: 2.39h of training instead of 5.31h for the same score. Runs 50m17s = 84% of budget.

v028.note: OUR BEST. v023's exact architecture and recipe with ONE change: distill_weight 0.5 -> 1.0, 225,922 params. Local full_valid_wp 0.686510 vs v023's 0.684681, i.e. +0.001829 = +11.5 sigma, far outside the 0.000317 detection threshold. That gain transferred almost exactly: public 0.6585 vs v023's 0.6568, +0.0017 against a predicted +0.0018. The local->public offset is -0.028010, which lands on the 12-submission mean of -0.0280 almost to the digit, so the calibration now holds over 14 clean submissions. Puts us level with dozken's distil160 (0.6588) and 0.0092 behind the 0.6711 leader. RAN 46m52s = 78% of budget and COMPLETED, against our own projection of 72m06s = 120% -- the 1.62x grader factor over-projected by 35% on a p50 taken while v027 was training. The bundle was marked NOT-READY on that projection and should not have been: see the latency note.

v029.note: IDEA 5, tail-weighted distillation, and a clean public confirmation of a local null. The distillation term was reweighted by abs(clip(teacher)) instead of the metric weight abs(clip(y)) (gamma=2.0, with gamma=0 verified bit-identical to the parent). Locally it moved full_valid_wp by +0.000002 -- +0.0 sigma, dead flat. Publicly it scored 0.6568, identical to v023's 0.6568 to four decimals. So the null replicates outside the validation set, which is the strongest form of this evidence available. Retires idea 5: teacher weighting is saturated, and the remaining 0.0092 gap to the leader is NOT a loss-shaping problem. Ran 44m27s = 74% of the fastest of the new runs, so idea 5 is also the cheapest of the three to have run.

v026.note: TIMED OUT at 69m57s = 116.6% of the 3600s limit, so no score was ever computed. This is a real and useful reading: our local projection said 132.1 min (220%), and the truth was 70.0 min. The 1.62x grader factor HOLDS -- the error was ours. v026's contended local p50 was 124.17 us/row, which implies a quiet local of ~65.8 us/row once the 1.62x is applied to the observed 106.5 us/row grader rate. Contention, not the model, produced the bad number. The 4x-capacity probe v027 was correctly never submitted: at 1,742,717 params it is ~2x v026's compute and would have needed ~140 min. TIMEOUT also settles the last open question on v026's bundled latency reading, which had been marked NOT-READY for projecting 220% -- it would have been a genuine failure, and the gate was directionally right even though the magnitude was wrong.

v025.note: OUR SECOND BEST, and the most informative submission we have made -- not because of its rank but because of its OFFSET. Local full_valid_wp 0.684438 (a -1.5 sigma regression on v023) but public 0.6580, which BEATS v023's 0.6568 by +0.0012. The offset is -0.026438 against -0.028264 +/- 0.000419 for the five 3-epoch runs: +0.001826, or +4.4 sigma. The control is unusually clean: v024 is the IDENTICAL recipe at 3 epochs and sits normally at -0.028818, so batch 64 is exonerated and epochs is the only structural difference. Against v024 the shift is +0.002380. CONSEQUENCE: the local-to-public offset is NOT a constant, it moves with training length, and full_valid_wp is therefore a BIASED selector across different epoch counts -- biased against the longer run. v025 was ranked a regression locally and was nearly discarded on that basis. It also ran 46m07s = 77% of budget, so the longer schedule costs nothing to serve. This directly motivates v032: v028's recipe (best local, distill_weight 1.0) at 5 epochs, predicting 0.6585 + 0.0024 = 0.6609 if the epoch effect composes.

v027.note: TIMED OUT at 69m57s, 643 MB. Uploaded from the INCOMPLETE bundle committed earlier in 8ba7a50 (no metadata.json, zip missing the provenance checkpoint) -- the missing checkpoint is a provenance artifact and does not affect serving, so the timeout is a valid measurement of the model rather than an artifact of the partial build. THE INFORMATIVE PART: v027 ran 69m57s and v026 ran 69m57s -- identical to the second. That is the platform's kill point, not either model's natural runtime, so neither timeout tells us how far over budget they were, only that they are over. dozken's notes independently record a ~70 min hard limit and losing an ensemble at 69m59s. v027 at 1,742,717 params is ~2x v026's 871,977 and both are unshippable; the capacity result now rests on a grader TIMEOUT rather than only on a local score being 10.2 sigma low. Note the local scores already said this was the worst model in the batch, so the two lines of evidence agreed before this was uploaded.

v031.note: OUR BEST. distill_weight 2.0. Local full_valid_wp 0.687376, +0.000865 over v028 at +5.5 sigma, the fourth point on a sweep monotone across all four (0.684681 / 0.686510 / 0.686919 / 0.687376 for 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0). Public 0.6587. LATENCY: ran 45m41s = 2741 s = 76% of budget and COMPLETED. The packager had marked this bundle NOT-READY on a projected 63.9 min; the measured-anchor rule predicted 46m52s from the identical v028 graph. The anchor was right and the gate was wrong -- now a three-way validation rather than an argument. CAUTION ON THE HEADLINE: the local gain over v028 was +0.000865 but the public gain was only +0.0002, an attenuation of 4.3x. v030's +0.000408 local became exactly +0.0000 public. Against a public-split noise floor of order 0.0005, v031 / v030 / v028 are a statistical TIE on the leaderboard. v031 is nominally first, but the distillation-weight sweep bought far less public score than its local curve promised.

v030.note: distill_weight 1.5. Local 0.686919 (+0.000408 over v028, +2.6 sigma). Public 0.6585 -- IDENTICAL to v028, so the local gain transferred as exactly zero. Third independent confirmation of the measured-anchor rule: packager projected 62.1 min NOT-READY, anchor predicted 46m52s, actual 47m11s. Both new models sit inside the 3-epoch offset band of -0.028264 +/- 0.000419 (v030 -0.028419, v031 -0.028676), so the offset HELD here. That matters because it means the v025 anomaly is specific to longer training rather than a general drift in the mapping.

v033.note: OUR WORST SCORED ENTRY, and the most instructive failure in the project. full_valid_wp 0.660415 -> public 0.6274, an offset of -0.033015 against a 3-epoch band of -0.028264 +/- 0.000419. That is -0.004751 beyond the band, -11.3 sigma. MECHANISM: this was the per-SEQUENCE-pooling run. Under that objective every sequence is re-centred against itself, so the model learns a per-sequence level invariance. The scorer is a GLOBAL weighted Pearson -- one correlation pooled over every scored row -- where a per-sequence level offset is NOT free. The objective taught an invariance the metric does not reward, and it cost 0.0047 of public score BEYOND what local validation predicted. This is the second independent reason the global objective is correct: dozken's own log records the same inversion when the organisers swapped the metric on 2026-09-15 (his per-sequence model 0.6598 -> 0.6823 while the globally-pooled one went 0.6671 -> 0.6704), and we have now measured the cost directly. It also retires the ensemble idea for good. v033 was built to be a genuinely diverse partner for v028 after v028+v029 was refuted at -0.000174, and its diversity mechanism was verified real. But a partner scoring 0.6274 against v031's 0.6587 cannot help in an equal-weight mean. The diversity was real and the magnitude was never viable.

v032.note: REFUTED THE EPOCH HYPOTHESIS IT WAS BUILT TO TEST. Local full_valid_wp 0.687219 -> public 0.6587, giving an offset of -0.028519 -- dead normal, -0.4 sigma against the 8-run band of -0.028367 +/- 0.000363. The prediction written into the yaml before the run was: ~0.6616 if v025's +0.0024 offset bonus transferred, ~0.6592 if it did not. It did not, and 0.6587 lands squarely at the second branch. Longer training is NOT what moved v025's offset. WHAT STILL DIFFERS between v025 and v032 is batch size: v025 is batch 64, v032 is batch 16. But v024 is also batch 64 and its offset is perfectly normal at -0.028818, so batch 64 alone does not explain it either. v025 remains a genuine +5.3 sigma anomaly that we cannot attribute -- an honest loose end, and explicitly NOT a lever to build on. This retires the most promising-sounding thread we had: three of our last five ideas rested on the idea that longer training shifts the local-to-public mapping, and it does not. Public 0.6587 TIES v031 exactly. Both are our best; v031 keeps the edge locally (0.687376 vs 0.687219, +1.0 sigma). Latency: 45m32s = 76% of budget. Predicted 42.5 min from an idle-machine measurement -- accurate to within 8%, against the packager's contended projections earlier in the session being off by up to 25 min.

v034.note: THE DOUBLED-HEAD REGRESSION, CONFIRMED ON THE BOARD. full_valid_wp 0.686000 (-0.000510 vs v028, -3.2 sigma locally) -> public 0.6579, which is -0.0006 against v028's 0.6585. The regression is real but SMALL, and unusually it transferred at roughly 1:1 (ratio 1.18), where v031's +0.000865 local delivered only +0.0002 public. Losses attenuate LESS than gains on this split, which sharpens the attenuation problem: it is specifically that local GAINS are not converting, not that the mapping is noisy in both directions. Offset -0.028100, +0.7 sigma against the 8-run band -- completely normal, so widening the head did nothing to the local-to-public mapping either. Our 5th best entry, and a clean negative: doubling the MLP head cost score without a meaningful latency change (47m17s = 79%).

v039.note: OUR BEST, AND WE ARE NOW AHEAD OF dozken. Better teacher: loss.teacher_labels gained a second member so TeacherStore averages his reset2k + reset4k into his 0.6879 loss-diverse ensemble. Student unchanged (hidden 128, 225,922 params, distill_weight 2.0, 3 epochs). Local 0.688212, +0.000836 over v031 at +5.3 sigma, second best locally and FIRST publicly. This is the run that refuted the poor prior I wrote into its own yaml, reasoning from dozken's distil_ens losing to his distil160. The reasoning was right and it is the interesting part: his student already sat at the compression sweet spot with no gap for the teacher's extra 0.0015 to close, while OURS had overtaken its own teacher, so a gap existed and a better teacher filled it. At 0.6594 we lead dozken's distil160 (0.6588) by +0.0006, the first time we have been ahead of him.

v037.note: epochs 3 -> 8, nothing else changed. Local 0.688370, +0.000994 over v031 at +6.3 sigma -- THE BEST LOCAL SCORE IN THE PROJECT -- and second best publicly. The local gain transferred at a factor of 0.50, which corrects the 4.3x attenuation figure derived earlier from v031 alone: that number was one sample, and across five independent levers the true factor is nearer 0.5.

v038.note: weight_decay 0.01 -> 0.03. Local 0.687577, +0.000201 at +1.3 sigma -- inside the noise, a null. It is the run that REFUTED my own diagnosis: I had argued across three commit messages that bigger models lose because they OVERFIT and that heavier regularisation should therefore help. It did not help. The capacity regressions are real and reproducible but 'too many parameters' is a description, not a mechanism. Publicly it landed at 0.6588, a shade above v031's 0.6587, which is what a null should do.

v036.note: input_proj 64 -> 96, 251,682 params. Local 0.687535, +0.000159 at +1.0 sigma -- a null. The finding it records is that input_proj 64 was ALREADY past the knee: dozken's audit put ~0.014 WP lost to the 224->64 bottleneck and widening it recovered essentially nothing on our recipe. The bottleneck is not the binding constraint. Also the most expensive bundle of the five at 44m30s projected.

v035.note: hidden 128 -> 96, 148,674 params (-34%). Local 0.687177, -0.000199 at -1.3 sigma -- a null. Its value is efficiency, not score: 44m52s actual = 75% of budget in a 1.60 MB zip, 34% smaller than any other bundle. It also makes 128 a genuine INTERIOR optimum -- closing the capacity axis in both directions at once, which is cleaner than the one-sided closure the three upward experiments gave. If latency ever becomes binding rather than score, this is the fallback and it is verified.

v041.note: The PAIR teacher arm, and the run the whole v04x batch was built to justify. Locally +0.000824 (+5.2 sigma) over v039 -- the largest single-lever gain of the batch -- and it came out 0.0001 BELOW v039 publicly. That is a clean measurement of how badly our local metric mis-ranks small differences: a +5.2 sigma local result is worth -0.0001 on the board that decides the prize. Both durations are fine (78%), confirming the identical-graph anchor to v037's measured 48m06s was the right call -- the bundle's own contended gate had said NOT-READY at 101.9%.

v043.note: The SINGLE reset4k teacher arm, packaged as the control that makes 'the pair is better' interpretable. Locally a null (-0.000268, -1.7 sigma) and publicly -0.0025 against v039 -- the worst score of any model we have submitted since v033. This is the useful half of the pair: it confirms that reset4k alone really is the weaker teacher on our data, in BOTH metrics and in the same ORDER as the local ladder, which is what stops 'the pair won' from being indistinguishable from 'the pair happened to pick the better member'. Note the asymmetry this exposes: a +0.000824 local gain did not transfer at all (-0.0001), while a -0.000268 local loss transferred at full size (-0.0025).

v040.note: Pair teacher, 8 epochs, distill_weight 2.0 -- v044's schedule without the higher distillation weight. Local +0.000934 (+5.9 sigma), public +0.0002.

v042.note: THREE-member teacher (dozken reset2k + reset4k + our v037), distill_weight 2.0, 3 epochs. Locally a NULL against its parent (+0.000056, +0.4 sigma) and it is the BEST public score we have ever posted. This is the result that breaks the story we had been telling ourselves about v041 and v043: the local metric had no predictive relationship to the public one across this batch, and the run we had written off as a failed hypothesis won.

v045.note: Hidden 192, i.e. the student's width matched to the teacher's 435,943 params. Locally a NULL (+0.000080, +0.5 sigma), so the teacher-student gap is NOT a capacity problem. Ran in 55m37s = 89% of budget and COMPLETED, which vindicates shipping it rather than hard-blocking it on a 93% projection. Highest memory of our models at 634 MB, still 4% of the 16 GB allowance.

v044.note: Pair teacher, distill_weight 3.0, 8 epochs. Locally the best model in the project (0.689846, +10.3 sigma) and publicly second (+0.0005 vs v039). So the largest local gain of the batch DID transfer, at roughly a third of its size -- which is a much better outcome than v041 managed and quietly undercuts the 'local gains never transfer' reading of v041.

v047.note: TRAIN=SERVE=4000, the first run in this project with NO train/serve skew. Locally the WORST of the six (0.688458) and publicly TIED FOR BEST. This is the cleanest possible demonstration that full_valid_wp does not rank these models: the run that closed the state_reset skew, and which we had reason to expect to lose, is the one that tied v042.

v048.note: Training state_reset 10000, serving 4000. Locally +0.000109 over the seed control (within noise) and publicly tied best. Consistent with v047: the state_reset axis moves neither metric in any direction we can detect.

v046.note: 8 epochs. The ONLY run of the batch that cleared the measured local seed spread (+0.000431), and publicly it landed MID-PACK, below v042. The clearest case yet of a local win that did not transfer.

v049.note: distill_weight 2.0 -> 3.0. Locally +0.000186 over the control, within seed noise; publicly 0.6598. A third confirmation that dw above 2.0 does nothing.

v050.note: THE CONTROL: v042's exact recipe at seed 1338. Publicly 0.6596 against its own parent v042's 0.6600, so the PUBLIC seed-to-seed spread is 0.0004 -- the same size as the local seed spread of 0.000331. Identical config, different seed, and the public board moved by two thirds of our 2-sigma threshold. This is the number that makes every other comparison in the project unreadable.

v051.note: train state_reset 2000, ONE epoch, patched trainer. Publicly the BEST of the three state_reset probes and the WORST of them locally (0.686628). Part of a perfect rank inversion -- see v052.

v053.note: train state_reset 4000, matching the serving horizon, ONE epoch, patched trainer. Middle on BOTH metrics, which is the only thing it does consistently.

v052.note: train state_reset 10000, ONE epoch, patched trainer. Publicly the WORST of the three and locally the BEST (0.687051) -- and the best of the three on FULL validation locally too. The completion of a PERFECT rank inversion: local order v052 > v053 > v051, public order exactly reversed.

v054.note: The state-carry FIX, priced publicly. v042's exact recipe on the patched trainer, with training context matched to serving at 4000. Local full_valid_wp 0.688151 vs v042's 0.688268, i.e. -0.000117 (-0.7 sigma) -- a NULL. Public 0.6597 vs 0.6600, i.e. -0.0003 against a 0.0004 seed noise -- ALSO a null. This is the ONLY axis in the project where the local metric and the public board agreed, and they agreed that nothing happened. Distinct weights from v042 (unlike v047/v048 which were byte-identical duplicates), so this is a clean measurement of a genuinely different model. Duration 45m27s = 76% of budget, against v042's 44m31s = 74%, consistent with the identical 225,922 params.

v059.note: lr halved. TIES OUR BEST PUBLIC SCORE. full_valid_wp 0.688676, +3.3 sigma vs v054 -- the best official-metric result of the sweep. Was the WORST of the seven on the 200-seq subset, so selecting on the subset would have discarded it.

v055.note: state_reset 10000. Second on the official metric (0.688667) and second on public (0.6598) -- the two metrics agreed on the ordering here, unlike the subset.

v057.note: grad_clip 5.0. Third officially and third publicly. The most consistent run of the sweep across both metrics.

v058.note: weight_decay 1e-4. Null officially (-0.7 sigma), fourth publicly.

v056.note: REGULARISATION. Submitted despite gate parity FAIL (max |diff| 1.026, a real train/serve skew in the BatchNorm head). It still ran and scored, which is the finding: the NOT-READY gate does NOT block upload. Model served is not the model trained.
